items.title: Player interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2012
items.q: That band was Wallace Davenport; ... Joe Smith, Joseph Smith, we called him Joe Fox, played drums ... I really enjoyed my time working with Wallace Davenport. ... all of these gentleman that I played with at that time

ctx.x: Just to wrap up, do you have any fond memories of playing or recording or whatever, with any of the other notable New Orleans fellas, ladies? © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

Oh there’s so many great memories. I really enjoyed my time working with Wallace Davenport. I was speaking about him earlier. And I think I probably joined that band about ’96 I think, yeah, it was around ’96. And at that time he had a regular engagement at the Maison Bourbon Jazz Club. And all of these gentleman that I played with at that time, they were much older men. That band was Wallace Davenport; Ralph Johnson, who played tenor and saxophone and clarinet; Joe Smith, Joseph Smith, we called him Joe Fox,…
you call it, when you’re passing through, and you’re passing the torch and you’re coming of age. You know what I mean? It’s like this whole thing.
